newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, fronts pressured.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends mixed, fronts pressured.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended mixed on Friday in a sluggish, post-bidweek session, with front months, hit by technical selling and reports of softer cash, again unable to get above unchanged, sources said.
Spot-July slipped 1.1 cents to close at $2.239 per million British thermal units. August settled 0.9 cent lower at $2.242. But most other months ended steady to up by one cent.

"The market looked a little heavy. We've got more mild weather next week and the perception is everyone is long, but I don't see it selling off too far," said one Texas trader, adding hot weather later next month should revive the rally.
While some traders expected mild weather next week to pressure both cash and paper early in the month, others said steady injection demand and more Southwest heat should limit the downside.

"This week we let some of the air out of the tires (of the recent rally), but even with the (mild) forecast next week, I think we'll trade in the same range (between $2.20 and $2.35)," said another Texas trader.

But chart traders grew more negative Friday after July's close below trendline support. Some now expected a test of the $2.17 area, with next support likely at around $2.09. Resistance was seen first at $2.25, then at $2.37-2.38 and at the contract high of $2.44.

In the cash, June Gulf Coast prices notionally slipped by five cents Friday to the low-$2.20s. June Midcon gas fell a similar amount to about $2.05. New York city gate prices lost a nickel or more to the low-to-mid $2.40s.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 0.2 cent to $2.257. NYMEX said 24,859 contracts traded, down from Thursday's revised tally of 30,191.

On the KCBT, July finished 0.3 cent lower at $2.104, while deferreds ended down by one-half to three cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.8 cent to 13.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 297 lots traded, up from Thursday's total of 140.
